parts.visual:
Imposter Syndrome is the internal psychological experience of feeling like a phony, despite evidence of success. It affects over 70% of high-achieving executives.

Overcoming it:
1. Separate feelings from facts (Look at your actual track record).
2. Normalize it (Realize your peers feel it too).
3. Reframe 'I don't know' as 'I am capable of learning'.
parts.audio: Imposter Syndrome affects over 70% of high-achieving executives. Separate your feelings from facts and reframe 'I don't know' as 'I can learn'.

questions.question: An executive is promoted and thinks: 'They made a mistake, I am not qualified for this.' This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Discounting objective evidence of competence (like a promotion) is the classic hallmark of imposter syndrome.

questions.question: Listen to the phrase. What mental shift is the leader making?
questions.tts_text: I may not have all the answers right now, but I have the resources and the team to figure it out.
options: Reframing self-doubt into a growth mindset.
questions.correct_answer: Reframing self-doubt into a growth mindset.
questions.explanation: Executives are not paid to know everything instantly; they are paid to navigate uncertainty effectively.

questions.question: Why is 'Perfectionism' often linked to Imposter Syndrome?
options: Because perfection is required in business.
Because perfectionists set impossibly high standards, guaranteeing they will eventually 'fail' and feel like imposters.
Because it makes you work faster.
questions.correct_answer: Because perfectionists set impossibly high standards, guaranteeing they will eventually 'fail' and feel like imposters.
questions.explanation: Perfection is the enemy of progress. Executive leadership requires acting on 80% of the information.

questions.question: How can a leader help their team overcome Imposter Syndrome?
options: Openly share their own past failures and moments of doubt to normalize the experience.
questions.correct_answer: Openly share their own past failures and moments of doubt to normalize the experience.
questions.explanation: Vulnerability from the top creates psychological safety, allowing the team to stop hiding their insecurities and start working.
